**2.** (a) $H_0$: The agent is meeting the licensing regulations. $H_A$: The agent is in gross violation of the licensing regulations. (b) Concluding the agent is in gross violation, and revoking his license, when he is actually meeting the regulations. (c) Concluding the agent is meeting the regulations, leaving his license intact, when he is actually in gross violation. (d) Type I — he loses his license, and his livelihood, despite complying. (e) Type II — the clubs keep receiving doctored dossiers from an agent who kept his license. (f) Strong evidence — demanding very strong evidence raises the Type II risk, so a violating agent would more often keep his license and keep feeding clubs inflated dossiers.

**4.** (a) True — the 99% interval is wider than, and contains, the 95% interval built from the same data. (b) False — decreasing $\alpha$ *decreases* the probability of a Type I error, since that probability equals $\alpha.$ (c) False — failing to reject $H_0$ means the data provide insufficient evidence against $p = 0.5,$ not that $p = 0.5$ is true. (d) True.

**6.** Decrease — with $n = 500$ the standard error shrinks (by a factor of $\sqrt{10}$), so the unchanged sample proportion sits further from the null value in standard-error units, giving a larger test statistic and a smaller p-value.

**8.** (a) Type II errors — if the null were true, only about $20 \times 0.05 = 1$ of the twenty trials should reject, so twelve rejections point to a genuine difference, and the eight analysts who failed to reject likely made Type II errors in underpowered trials. (b) Answers vary; key: pool into one larger, higher-power trial.

**10.** (a) $H_0: p = 0.2$; $H_A: p > 0.2,$ where $p$ is the proportion of pre-test questions that new academy intakes answer correctly. (b) $H_0: p = 0.32$; $H_A: p \neq 0.32,$ where $p$ is the proportion of players on the new protocol who return to full training within three weeks of a soft-tissue injury. (c) $H_0: p = 0.67$; $H_A: p > 0.67,$ where $p$ is the proportion of season-ticket holders who renew in the coming window.
